tool.name: dDocent Filters
tool.description: filter a FreeBayes VCF from dDocent

param.name: vcf
param.label: FreeBayes VCF file from dDocent
param.help: This is the Final.recode.vcf produced by the dDocent pipeline.

param.label: Do the reads of a fragment overlap?
param.help: That is, is the fragment size less than twice the read length? With overlapping reads both read pairs cover the same bases, so the forward/reverse read balance filters must be skipped.
param.option: No - fragments are longer than 2x the read length
Yes - reads overlap within a fragment

param.label: Is this a mixture of single-end and paired-end libraries?
param.help: With mixed libraries the properly-paired filter is replaced by a tag-based one, because single-end reads are never marked as properly paired.
param.option: No - all libraries have the same layout
Yes - single-end and paired-end libraries are mixed

param.label: Maximum mean depth cutoff
param.help: Sites with an average depth above the cutoff are dropped; highly covered sites are usually collapsed repeats. The automatic cutoff is the 95th percentile of the mean depth per site, rounded down to an integer; dDocent prints the histogram of the observed mean depth per site so the choice can be checked.
param.option: Automatic (95th percentile of the mean depth)

has_text.text: Histogram of mean depth per site

tool.help:
What it does ------------
``dDocent_filters`` applies dDocent's recommended post-processing filters to the FreeBayes VCF file produced by the dDocent pipeline tool. The filters are applied in this order:
1. **Allele balance, locus quality and mapping quality** - heterozygous genotypes must have an allele balance between 0.2 and 0.8 (or close to 0/1), the reference and alternate allele qualities (``QR``/``QA``) must be non-zero, ``QUAL / DP`` must exceed 0.1, and the forward/reverse mapping qualities (``MQM``/``MQMR``) must be balanced. 2. **Overlapping reads** - only when the reads of a fragment overlap: loci must be supported by both strands with comparable forward and reverse coverage (``SAF``/``SAR``/``SRF``/``SRR``). With fragments longer than twice the read length this filter is skipped, because the two reads then cover different bases. 3. **Properly paired reads** - loci must be supported by a comparable share of properly paired reads (``PAIRED``/``PAIREDR``). For a mixture of single-end and paired-end libraries the equivalent tag-based filter is used instead, because single-end reads are never flagged as properly paired. 4. **High depth with low quality** - loci whose depth is above the mean plus one standard deviation and whose ``QUAL`` is below twice that depth are removed. 5. **Maximum mean depth** - loci whose mean depth exceeds the cutoff are removed; highly covered sites are usually collapsed repeats. 6. **Within-locus depth mismatch** - individuals whose depth at a locus is below 60% of the mean depth of that locus are dropped, which removes loci with a badly unbalanced coverage across individuals.
Input -----
The VCF file written by the dDocent pipeline (``Final.recode.vcf``), i.e. a FreeBayes file that still carries the ``NS``, ``DP``, ``MQM``, ``MQMR``, ``PAIRED`` or ``PAIREDR`` statistics. A VCF that has been re-processed by other tools may lack these fields and will then be filtered into nothing.
Outputs -------
* the filtered VCF (``<prefix>.FIL.recode.vcf``), * a plain-text report (``<prefix>.filterstats``) with the number of sites removed by each step, the ASCII histogram of the mean depth per site and the cutoff that was used.
If every site is removed the tool fails instead of returning an empty VCF: that happens when the input was already filtered once, or when the answers about the read layout are wrong, and it is not what a run of this tool should produce.
